name: pengdows.crud
method: Members come from the IL of the consumer's own assembly (every call, callvirt, newobj and ldftn naming a System.Data member, with the line from its PDB), plus reflection through nameof(DbDataReader.X), GetSchema collection names, CommandBehavior flags and the using statements that dispose a command, connection, reader or transaction. A Required test is included when the consumer calls its member; a Common or Optional test only when the consumer relies on that behavior, which "because" explains.

tests.because: A null value is sent as DBNull.Value.
The maintenance probe sets a timeout; today a refusal is caught and the probe skipped (a workaround).
Prepare on an open connection must work or be a no-op; today an exception disables preparing for the connection (a workaround).
A prepared command is executed again with new values.
A prepared command is reused with new text.
The dialect reads its parameter marker from DataSourceInformation; today a missing collection falls back to SQL-92 defaults (a workaround).
The advertised marker is used to write SQL.
Connection strings are read and written through the provider builder; today a missing builder is skipped (a workaround).
A failed statement is recognised as a DbException; today AseException, which is not one, is recognised by name (a workaround).
NULL is read as DBNull.Value; today a C# null is accepted too (a workaround).
A reused decimal parameter must carry a wider value exactly; today Precision and Scale are widened by hand (a workaround).
pengdows.crud works around this today: Setting Connection to null on a command that has run is wrapped in a try: Snowflake, SQLite and others throw.
pengdows.crud works around this today: Disposing a command is wrapped in a try that logs and carries on (Microsoft.Data.Sqlite throws).
pengdows.crud works around this today: Disposing a command is wrapped in a try that logs and carries on (Microsoft.Data.Sqlite throws).
pengdows.crud works around this today: ResetDbType on a pooled parameter is wrapped in a try for providers that do not support it.

excluded.because: Commands are only executed on an open connection.
Commands are only executed with a connection set.
Prepare is only called on an open connection.
Prepare is only called on a command with an open connection.
RemoveAt is only called with the index of a parameter the command has (SqlDialect.ReplaceArgumentWithNull).
RemoveAt is only called with the index of a parameter the command has (SqlDialect.ReplaceArgumentWithNull).
Every parameter gets its name before use (SqlDialect.CreateDbParameter).
Every parameter gets its name before use (SqlDialect.CreateDbParameter).
Every parameter gets its value before use (SqlDialect.CreateDbParameter).

workarounds.what: Setting Connection to null on a command that has run is wrapped in a try: Snowflake, SQLite and others throw.
Disposing a command is wrapped in a try that logs and carries on (Microsoft.Data.Sqlite throws).
A NullReferenceException from disposing a prepared MySql.Data command after EOF is treated as a clean dispose.
Removing the StateChange handler after Dispose catches ObjectDisposedException (AdoNetCore.AseClient).
A provider error that is not a DbException is recognised by its type name (AdoNetCore.AseClient AseException).
A NULL read as C# null instead of DBNull.Value is accepted.
A reused decimal parameter has its Precision and Scale widened by hand before a wider value is sent (SAP HANA).
An exception from Prepare disables preparing for that connection and the command runs unprepared.
A refused CommandTimeout skips the maintenance probe.
Without DataSourceInformation the dialect uses SQL-92 defaults and its own constants.
A factory without a connection string builder is skipped when the connection string is read.
ResetDbType on a pooled parameter is wrapped in a try for providers that do not support it.
Resetting a pooled parameter to DbType.Object is dropped for a provider that rejects it (Informix).
GetValue, GetDateTime and GetFieldType on a timestamp column fall back to GetFieldValue<DateTime> (Npgsql 9).
A Guid column the provider cannot return is read from its bytes (Npgsql on Spanner uuid).
An array the provider refuses as T[] is read as an array of nullable elements (Npgsql on Spanner).
An integer that overflows Int64 is read back from its text.
A NUMBER beyond decimal falls back to GetDouble.
A timestamp with time zone the provider reports as DateTime is read through GetValue or GetDateTimeOffset (Snowflake.Data, ODP.NET 21).
